beats.narration: Your eval now tells you what good looks like, as a number. What it cannot tell you is where a failure happened. That takes two more layers: tests that isolate each failure type, and traces that point at the exact step that broke.

elements.text: the eval says HOW GOOD — not WHERE it broke

beats.narration: Four test levels, each catching a break the others miss. A unit test isolates one function — a parser, a tool wrapper — and says nothing about how pieces fit. A functional test checks that one model call returns the expected shape. An integration test exercises the handoff between two components, like retrieval passing into the model call. And an end-to-end test runs the whole flow the way a user would. It catches everything and localizes nothing. Keep your eye on the third level: most silent production breaks live at the seams.

items.text: functional — one call returns the right shape
end-to-end — whole flow: catches all, localizes none

elements.text: silent breaks live at the SEAMS

beats.narration: Tests say a failure exists. A trace says where. It records every step of a run — the prompt, the tool calls, the intermediate outputs, the timing. Read this one top to bottom: retrieval, fine. Prompt build, fine. Model call, fine. Step four, the parser, raises a key error on a field the model never returned. One glance and the failure is localized. That's the difference between a five-minute fix and a day spent walking the workflow by hand.

elements.text: the trace: a timeline of the run

elements.code:
step 1  retrieve(query)       ok    ->  3 chunks
step 2  build_prompt(chunks)  ok    ->  1,240 tok
step 3  model.call(prompt)    ok    ->  answer "..."
step 4  parse(answer)         FAIL  ->  KeyError: amount

elements.text: 5-minute fix  vs  a day of guessing

beats.narration: One more pattern, for mixed traffic: routing. A cheap classification call reads each query and picks a path. Single-fact lookups take the fetch-once path. Multi-part questions take search across rounds. Default everything to iterative search and you inflate cost on questions one fetch would answer. Default everything to a static index and you get shallow answers where several passes were needed. And if all your traffic is one shape, skip the router and hardcode the path.

elements.text: routing: pay for iteration only when needed

wrong default: iterative-everything = cost,
static-everything = shallow answers

beats.narration: Here's the seam failure in the wild. Every unit test green. The functional test green. End-to-end: red. The trace shows why: retrieval returns a list of chunk dictionaries, and the prompt builder expected a plain string. The context arrived malformed, so the model quietly answered from its own memory instead of the retrieved policy. Each side was correct in isolation. The contract between them was never defined, and no test ever drove the two together. Only an integration test on that exact handoff — real chunks into the real builder — surfaces the mismatch before a user does.

elements.text: watch out: pieces passed, the seam broke

elements.code:
PASS  test_parser_unit
PASS  test_extract_shape_functional
FAIL  test_full_flow_e2e
  cause: retrieve() -> [{"content": ...}]
         build_prompt() expected a string

elements.text: model answered from MEMORY, not the docs
✓ one integration test on the handoff = caught

beats.narration: The reflex: when the pieces pass and the flow fails, look at the seams — then put a test on every handoff you find. Next, the checkpoint hands you a trace to diagnose. After that: failure handling and model selection.

elements.text:
pieces pass + flow fails → check the SEAMS,
then test every handoff
